criteria.no: A new decision or a different demand.
criteria.unclear: Cannot tell whether a detail is obvious precision or a new decision.
criteria.yes: Same demand as the quote, at most obviously more precise.

faithful.instructions: Does `anchor.statement` ask for the same thing as `anchor.quote`? Obvious precise readings are the same thing (must for should; stdout for where a CLI prints; subcommands for a CLI's commands; one directive selected from several; the same named records; illustrative values for a described test). A new decision the quote leaves open (algorithm, strength, count, tool, trigger) or a different demand is not. Do not judge vagueness, bundling, or scope.

criteria.no: At least one required outcome rests on something subjective, undefined, or unidentified.
criteria.unclear: An outcome is partly concrete but what to inspect cannot be determined, with nothing undefined or unidentified.
criteria.yes: Each required outcome has something concrete or an identified record to inspect.

observable.instructions: Step 1: list each outcome `anchor.statement` requires. Step 2: for each, name what a reviewer would inspect (behavior, output, exit status, file, path, value, tool use, or an identified record). Step 3: if any outcome has nothing nameable to inspect because it rests on a subjective quality, an undefined label/tier/mode, or an unidentified baseline, expected output, approval, or standard, answer no. Inline definitions and inline exception lists count as inspectable. Ignore bundling and style.

criteria.unclear: A subject is hinted at but cannot be identified.

scoped.instructions: Name the subject that `anchor.statement` or `anchor.scope` constrains (command, module, service, pipeline, artifact, process, path, or explicit all/every set). If one is named, the answer is yes regardless of requirement quality.

criteria.no: A decisive term is subjective, undefined, unidentified, or an unrecorded approval.
criteria.unclear: A term may not be understood, but it cannot be told whether it is decisive.
criteria.yes: Every decisive term is understood without outside context.

self_contained.instructions: Could an engineer with common technical knowledge and no other context understand every decisive term of `anchor.statement`? Commands, flags, files, paths, values, formats, streams, roles, named releases/tags/report ids, and inline-defined terms are understood. A subjective quality, an undefined label or mode, an unidentified baseline/expected output/standard, or an approval with no identified record is not, and one such decisive term makes the answer no. Ignore bundling, added details, form, and who acts.

criteria.no: Separate actions or subjects that could pass and fail independently.
criteria.unclear: Equally readable as one action with several targets or as separate actions.
criteria.yes: Single action or prohibition of one subject; lists only qualify it.

single_constraint.instructions: Imagine checking `anchor.statement`. Could one part pass while another fails because they are different actions or belong to different subjects? If every listed item only names a target, stream, file, value, or condition of one action or prohibition, it is a single constraint. Judge only that.

anchor.statement: The package may publish only when the release lead approves.
anchor.quote: only publish after the release lead says yes
